text:
maria: Heads-up — during a DSAR backfill QA run I noticed deletions for tenant `acme-corp` didn't remove older GCP snapshots. Appears the erasure job logged KMS decrypt failures for the snapshot objects. Need quick triage, possible KMS/RBAC gap.

arjun: Can you paste the exact error from the job logs? Also which service account is the erasure runner using? If it's missing `kms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` it would fail.

maria: Log excerpt from job (sanitized):
```
2026-03-20T10:12:45Z erasure-runner: delete snapshot gs://acme-backups/snap-20240101.tar.gz -> FAILED: 403 Permission denied: cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt for projects/redwood-prod/locations/us-central1/keyRings/erasure/cryptoKeys/snap-key/cryptoKeyVersions/1
```
Service account in use: `svc-erasure@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com`

lina: That matches the KMS permission issue. But before changing RBAC, confirm there are no active legal holds for this tenant. @sam any flags? :mag_right:

sam: I checked the legal queue — no active legal hold on acme-corp, nothing in the litigation tracker. If this was an ad-hoc retention exception previously approved, please attach the request ID. Otherwise privacy can greenlight remedial action.

arjun: Quick note: we should avoid granting broad storage or KMS roles. Proposed minimal role `roles/redwood.erasureRunner` with permissions: `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt`, `cloudkms.cryptoKeys.get`, `storage.objects.delete`, `storage.objects.get`, `storage.objects.getIamPolicy`.

maria: Agreed. Also noticed the failing snapshots were encrypted with an older key version (v1) while our rotation promoted v2. The erasure runner's key binding only referenced the new key version in IAM binding. That mismatch caused KMS to deny use on v1 objects.

erasure-bot: automated job report: `erasure-backfill-2026-03-20` -> 12/348 objects failed with KMS 403. Backoff scheduled, no further retries until manual ack.

lina: Action items I propose: 1) Create dedicated service account + custom role (arjun) 2) Grant that SA access to all key versions for relevant keyring (temporary scoped grant) 3) Run canary deletion in us-central1 only (maria) 4) Capture audit logs and snapshot key-access attempts (lina) 5) If manual deletion needed, legal to confirm no holds (sam) 6) File retention-exception if we need to quarantine snapshots (maria)

arjun: I'll create the SA + role; planning commands: 
```
# create SA
gcloud iam service-accounts create redwood-erasure-runner --project=redwood-prod
# create custom role (YAML is in infra/roles/erasure-runner.yaml)
gcloud iam roles create redwoodErasureRunner --project=redwood-prod --file=infra/roles/erasure-runner.yaml
# bind role to SA
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding redwood-prod --member=serviceAccount:redwood-erasure-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --role=projects/redwood-prod/roles/redwoodErasureRunner
```
I'll also add a temporary binding to ensure `cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` applies to all versions: `gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding ... --member=serviceAccount:...`

maria: For the canary, I'll target a small prefix `gs://acme-backups/canary/*` and log verbosely. If canary passes, we can roll region-by-region. Please ensure the erasure-runner SA is restricted to only the keyring used by snapshots (not all KMS keys).

sam: If you need a retention-exception, use the internal form and reference `REQ-2026-` prefix. Privacy will expedite if you include exact object paths, snapshot IDs, and justification (operational rollback risk). Also note legal hold take precedence; if legal later asserts a hold we will stop.

lina: For audit logs: enable `dataAccess` logs for KMS and Storage on the project for the next 14 days, and set an alert in Console -> Logging for `protoPayload.serviceName="cloudkms.googleapis.com" AND protoPayload.methodName:"AsymmetricDecrypt"` (or `cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt`). I'll create a temporary logsink to `logging-archive` bucket.

arjun: One more nuance — the erasure job uses cached object metadata listing which may reference old location links (regional snapshots). We'll run a discovery job to list all snapshots created between 2024-12-01 and 2025-02-01 to ensure coverage before mass delete. Command: `gsutil ls -r gs://acme-backups/** | grep snap-2024` (we'll replace with structured inventory soon).

maria: I'll also add a step in the runbook to check KMS key version bindings before backfills: `scripts/check-kms-bindings.sh --keyring=erasure --project=redwood-prod` and fail fast if binding doesn't cover versions. PR will reference infra PR #4321.

arjun: I'll provision the SA and post the IAM binding diff here when done. Expect a short maintenance window — propose 2026-03-22 18:00 UTC for canary run. If all green, full backfill resume 2026-03-23 morning UTC.

sam: Confirmed — privacy ok to proceed with canary at that window, provided logs are captured and retention-exception filed if we quarantine objects.

maria: Filed retention-exception placeholder: REQ-2026-045 (details to follow). Leaving this thread open for status updates. If anyone sees a legal hold pop up please ping immediately.

lina: I've created the logsink and enabled dataAccess for KMS/Storage, alert rule in place. PRs:
- infra#4321 (role + SA)
- docs#214 (runbook update)

arjun: SA + role created, binding applied (diff posted): `projects/redwood-prod/iamPolicy: + serviceAccount:redwood-erasure-runner@... -> roles/redwoodErasureRunner`. Will rotate IAM binder to least privilege after canary.

maria: Canary started, verbose logs enabled. Running on prefix `canary/` now.

erasure-bot: canary run report: 4 objects processed -> 0 failures. KMS decrypt succeeded for v1 and v2 for SA `redwood-erasure-runner`.

maria: Canary success. Plan: schedule region-by-region resume 03-23. I'll open a follow-up thread for postbackfill verification and metrics. Closing this triage thread; moving action items to the incident board.
